<gal>, war, with <mat>, seize: a person taken in war; {galmat suak}, go into captivity
<galmat> captive with <in>; in the state of a prisoner of war, with verbs of carrying off or being
plural of <galmat>, people taken in war
<gal>, enemy, with <mi>, person; {galmi et} is look on someone as an enemy, with ill will
safe from enemies and trouble, from <gal>, enemy, and <muang>, trust; paired with <lungmuang>, at ease

terms: see from afar/see at a distance
definition: <gal>, across or far off, with <muh>, see
<galmuh>, see from afar, with the linking suffix <in>

terms: be visible from afar/can be seen from a distance
definition: <galmuh> and <thei> written as one word, usually after <ki>: it can be seen from far away
Going to the house of a dead person to mourn with the family, used in the phrase {si galna}; Ecclesiastes sets it against {pawi simna}, going to a feast.
what is given to the family of a dead person in sympathy, mostly money, as {galna sum}, condolence money, and {galna pia}, give condolence; not the visit itself
<Gal>, enemy, with <nan>, withstand, and the noun suffix <na>: what is used to withstand an enemy, such as armor; {galnan'na kulh} is a stronghold.
<Gal>, enemy, with <nan>, withstand, and the noun suffix <na>: defence against an enemy; {galnanna kulh} is a fortified wall, a stronghold.
<gal>, enemy, with <neih>, have, written as one word: have someone as an enemy; with <ki>, be enemies of each other
<Gal>, enemy, with <neih>, have, and the noun suffix <na>: holding someone as an enemy; {galneihna bangmah nei lo} means having no malice toward someone.
<Gal>, enemy, with <pa>, which marks a man: the enemy, a male foe.
<Gal>, war, with <pan>, take a stand, and the noun suffix <na>: a place where soldiers take up position; {galpan'na mun} is a stronghold and {galpan'na phual} a military camp.
<Gal>, war, with <pan>, take a stand, and <mun>, place: a strong place to fight from.
<Gal>, war, with <pan>, take up a position, and the noun suffix <na>: a place held by soldiers; {galpanna mun} is a stronghold or outpost and {galpanna phual} a military camp.
<Gal>, war, with <phual>, place: the place where the fighting is.
a post where the soldiers of an army are stationed, which is attacked, taken or left; in war news after the name of an army, as {SAC galphual}, and often explained by <Camp>

terms: set up camp/pitch camp/establish a base
definition: <galphual>, military camp, as the object of <sat.2>, set up: troops pitch their camp or set up a base at a place; the place stands before it with <ah>, and <sat> here is neither strike nor decide

terms: to the battle/in battle/on the battlefield
definition: {Galphual}, battlefield, with the place marker <ah>: to or on the battlefield, into battle.
<galphual>, place of battle, with <pi>, great: a large or main military base or camp
plural of <galphual>: in news the camps and positions held by an army
<Gal>, war, with <pi>, great: a great war.
<galpi>, great war, and <khatna>, first: the First World War, also written {Leitung galpi khatna}; the Second World War is <galpi nihna>

<galpi>, great war, and <nihna>, second: the Second World War, 1939 to 1945, often written with capitals; {galpi nihna lai in} is during the Second World War, and the First World War is <galpi khatna>

<galpi>, great war, and <thumna>, third: a third world war, spoken of as a danger to come, often written with capitals and also as {Leitung galpi thumna}; the earlier ones are <galpi khatna> and <galpi nihna>
<galpi>, great war, with <nih>, two, written as one word: the Second World War; {galpinih hunlai in} is at the time of the Second World War
<galpi>, great war, and <nihna>, second, written as one word: the Second World War, often as {leitung galpinihna} or {leitungbup galpinihna}
<Gal>, from far off, with <sap>, call: call out to someone who is at a distance.
<Gal>, war, with <siam>, skilled: trained and able in fighting; {galsiam mi} is a skilled warrior.
<Gal>, enemy or war, with <sim>, attack: go to war, go into battle; also used like a noun for battle, as in {galsim mite}, fighting men.
{Galsim}, go to war, with the linking suffix <in>: going to war, followed by the next action.
{Galsim}, go to war, with the noun suffix <na>: an act or occasion of going out to fight, a raid, battle or campaign.
Plural of <galsimna>: the wars or campaigns that someone has fought.
{Galsim}, go to war, with <pih>, together with: join someone in battle.
{Galsim}, go to war, with the plural <te>: those who go out to attack, raiding parties.
{Galsim}, go to war, with <zia>, manner: the way to fight, the skill of war.
<gal> and <suak.2> written as one word: become war or enmity; the saying <ciamnuih galsuak> is a joke turns into a fight
<Gal>, war, with <sung>, inside: the battle or the war as the place one is in; {galsung pan} is from the battle and {galsung nazatte} are weapons of war.
{Galsung}, battle, with the place ending <a>: in battle; {galsunga site} are those who die in battle.
<Gal>, enemy, with <tai>, flee: a person who flees from an enemy or from war; {galtai-in} means as a fugitive, in flight.
A person who has fled from war to find safety in another place.
used as a verb, often before <uh> or <hi>: flee from fighting or persecution, where the other senses name the person who flees
<galtai>, flee from fighting, and <khia>, out, written as one word: flee out of a place because of war; also those who have fled
<galtai> and <mi> written as one word: a person who has fled from war, a refugee
{Galtai}, flee from the enemy, with the noun suffix <na>: fleeing before enemies.
Plural of <galtai>: people who flee from an enemy or from war.
Plural of <gal>: enemies, those who fight against or hate someone.
<gal>, war, with <vai>, affair: all that has to do with war and armed forces; {galvai tawh kisai} is concerning military matters, and it is paired with <gamvai> in the news sense of political affairs
<Gal>, war, with <van>, goods: the equipment of war, weapons and armor; {galvan koihna} is an armory and {galvan puapa} an armor-bearer.
<galvan>, weapons, and <tawi>, carry: carrying weapons, armed; it stands before the noun it describes, as {galvan tawi galkapte}, armed soldiers, like {thau tawi}, carrying guns
<gal>, war, with <vanleng>, aircraft: an aircraft of an armed force
plural of <galvanleng>
{Galvan} with the plural <te>: the things worn and carried for battle.
{Galvan}, weapons, with <teng>, all: all the weapons of a soldier.

terms: be at peace/fighting dies down/war is over
definition: <gal>, war, and <ven>, cease, written as one word: the war or the fighting is over or has died down; {galven hun} is a time of peace

terms: stand guard/be on guard/be on the alert
definition: keep watch against an enemy, said of armed forces holding a position

terms: the fighting ends/the quarrel is over
definition: <gal>, war or strife, and <veng>, cease, written as one word: a war or a quarrel comes to an end
<Gal>, enemy, with <vil>, watch: one who keeps watch for the enemy; also the act of keeping watch, as in {galvil koih}, post a guard.
used as a verb: keep watch against an enemy or over a place, with verb endings such as <sak> or {zel ni} after it, where the other sense names the watchman
{Galvil}, keep watch, with the noun suffix <na>: keeping watch against an enemy, or the place for it; {galvilna bukno} is a watchtower and {galvilna inndei} a guardroom.
{Galvil}, watch, with <pa>, which marks a man: a man who keeps watch for the enemy.
Plural of <galvil>: watchmen or guards who keep watch for the enemy.
<Gal>, from far off, with <zak>, hear: hear about someone or something that is elsewhere.
<Gal>, war, with <zawh>, the form of <zo>, overcome, used before another word; {galzawh van} is plunder, the goods won in war.
{Galzawh}, win in war, with the noun suffix <na>: victory in battle.

terms: win the war/be victorious in war/conquer
definition: <gal>, war, with <zo>, win, written as one word; also said of the side that has won
<Gal>, war, with <zo>, win, and the plural <te>: those who win a war.
<Gal>, from afar, with <zuih>, follow: follow at a distance; {nung galzuih} is follow behind someone from far off.
A country or region with its people; {mualtung gam} is hill country.
The area of land that belongs to a people, a tribe or a ruler.
The land that a king rules; {kumpi gam} is a kingdom.
Land as the place where people live; after a name it means the land of, as in {Kanaan gam}, the land of Canaan.
{Gam} written with a capital for the kingdom of God or of heaven, as in {Pasian’ Gam} and {Vantung Gam}.
<gam>, country, with <it>, love: loving one’s country, said of leaders and soldiers
<gam>, country, and <khangtote>, the developed ones: the developed countries of the world as a group, mostly followed by <ah> or <sung>
{Gam Kigawm}, united lands, with <Kawlgam> and <Kumpi>: the Union of Burma, so called because independence was gained only when the peoples of the country agreed together
the day of those who died for the country, one of the national days of Myanmar that the page lists
<gam>, the wild, and <ak>, fowl: the wild fowl of the forest; given by the book as a noun joined to a noun
<Gam>, wild country, with <bawngtal>, bull: a wild ox; also written <gambawngtal>.
<Gam> with the ending <a>, which joins the land to the word that follows: of or in that land.
place, of uncertain location, whose men guarded the towers of Tyre
<Gam> with the place marker <ah>: in or to the land of.

terms: in the kingdom/into the kingdom/in the land
definition: <Gam>, the capitalised word for kingdom or land, with <ah>, the marker of place: in or into the Kingdom, as in {Vantung Gamah}, in the kingdom of heaven.
name of two men: the son of Pedahzur, leader of the tribe of Manasseh in the wilderness, and a Pharisee and teacher of the law in Jerusalem
<Gam>, wild country, with <bawngtal>, bull: a wild ox that cannot be made to work.
<gam>, country, with <bel>, take refuge in: a person who seeks shelter in another country, and the status of such a person; named beside <galtai>, one who flees from war; also written <gambel>
<gambeel>, refugee, and <hihna>, the fact of being: the recognised standing of a refugee; mostly before <card>, the refugee card of the UNHCR, or <khensatna>, the decision on refugee status
people who take refuge in a country that is not their own, said of refugees and of immigrants; <gambeel> with the plural <te>
<gam>, country, and <bek>, only, written as one word; {gambek hilo} after a name is not only that country
<gam>, country, with <bel>, take refuge in: a person who has fled to another country and shelters there; often {gambel mi}

<gambel>, one who shelters in another country, and <galtai>, one who flees from war, two words of nearly the same meaning said together as one noun: a refugee; used of the people whose claim the UNHCR examines, and followed by <te> for the plural or <khat> for one
<gambel> and <ding> written as one word: in order to take refuge in another country, to be a refugee there
a person who takes refuge in another country; <gambel> with <mi>, person
<gambel>, refugee, with the plural <te>, written as one word
country in West Africa
<gam>, country, and <biakna>, religion, written as one word: the religion of a country; with <te>, those who hold to it
<gam>, country, and <bitna>, security, written as one word: the security or defence of a country
<gam>, country, and <buai>, be troubled, written as one word: a time when the country is in turmoil, through war or political crisis
<gam>, country, with <buaina>, trouble: the turmoil or crisis of a country
Wild, empty country where no one goes; {lam lianpite gambulak suak} means the highways have become deserted.
<Gam>, land, with <bup>, whole: the whole of a land.
The whole extent of a country or region, from one border to the other.
before a noun, of or for the country as a whole and not one state or town, as in <gambup thukhunpi>, the national constitution, and {gambup dawl}, the national level

<gambup>, the whole country, and <huam>, take in: covering the whole country, nationwide; stands before the noun it describes, or as a verb, reach the whole country; {minambup huam} is the same for a whole people

<gambup>, the whole country, and <huamin>, taking in: covering the whole country, nationwide; stands before the verb or the clause it qualifies, and a name may stand before it, as {ZBCA gambup huamin}, across the whole of ZBCA
<gambup>, the whole land, and <innpi>, great house: the parliament of the whole country, in Myanmar the Union Assembly, as distinct from the assembly of a state; often written with capitals

<gambup>, the whole country, and <kilemna>, peace: the peace of the whole union, the term for the peace process and the nationwide ceasefire agreement in Myanmar; often followed by <maban>, process, or <khawmpi>, conference
<gambup>, the whole country, and <kiteelna>, election: the election held across the whole country for its parliament, a general election; a year often stands before it
<gambup>, the whole country, and <kiteelpi>, a great election: the general election of a country; the year often stands before it
<gambup>, national, and <makaipi>, chief leader: the leader of the whole country, used for a president or head of government as against the leader of one state or party
<gambup>, the whole country, with <ni>, day: Union Day of Myanmar, kept every year on 12 February in memory of the agreement signed at Panglong in 1947
<gambup>, the whole country, with <suahtakna>, freedom: the independence of the whole of Burma from British rule; also listed as the name of a national day
<gambup>, the whole country, and <thukhunpi>, constitution: the constitution of a state, as against the constitution of an organisation; a year before or after it names one, {2008 gambup thukhunpi}

<gambup>, national, and <thuvanpi>, secretary: taken as the head of a parliamentary government, in {gambup thuvanpi makaihna ki-ukna}, parliamentary rule; found in one article title only, and the pair may name the parliament itself
<gambup> and <ah> written as one word: in the whole country

terms: in the whole land/on the whole land
definition: <Gam>, land, with <bup>, whole, the intensifier <pi> and the place marker <ah>: in or upon the whole land.
<gam>, country, and <ciat>, each, written as one word: each one his own country, as in {amau gamciat}, their respective countries
Still and without noise, said of a land at peace or of people who stop speaking; {gamdai takin} is quietly and {gamdai-in om} is keep silent.
Form of <gamdai>, quiet, used before <nading> and <khit>: become quiet, stop making noise.
{Gamdaih}, be quiet, with the noun suffix <na>: quiet country where no one is; often followed by <mun>, place.
the state of being quiet and not a place: the silence between people who do not speak, as in {gamdaihna sukham}, break the silence, or calm in a country, beside <lungmuanna>
{Gamdai}, quiet, with the causative <sak>: make people be quiet.
{Gamdaisak}, make quiet, with the linking suffix <in>: quieting people before going on to speak.
<gamdai> and <tak> written as one word, mostly with <in>: in a quiet and orderly way
{Gamdai}, quiet, with the comparative <zaw>: quieter than before.
<Gam>, land, with <dang>, other: of another country; {gamdang mi} is a foreigner or stranger and {gamdang pasian} a foreign god.
<Gam>, land, with <dang>, other: a land that is not one’s own; {gamdang khatah} is to another land.
<gamdang>, foreign country, with the ending <a>, in: in another country, abroad

terms: in a foreign land/to another land/among the nations/abroad
definition: {Gamdang}, foreign land, with the place marker <ah>: in or to another land, among other nations.
not a proper name: the word <gamdangah>, in a foreign land, written with a capital at the start of a sentence
{Gamdang}, foreign, with <mi>, person: a person from another country.
<gamdangmi>, foreigner, and <khualzin>, travel: a foreigner who travels in the country, a foreign tourist
<gamdangmi>, foreigner, and <nasem>, worker: a person from another country who works in the land, the term of the news for migrant labour in Malaysia
<gamdangmi>, foreigner, and <nasemte>, here workers and not servants: people from another country who work in a country, the term of the news for migrant labour
<gamdangmi>, foreigner, and <phalna>, permission: the official document that allows a foreigner to stay or work in a country; often with <neilo>, without valid papers
plural of <gamdangmi>: people from another country
<gamdang> and <pan> written as one word: from a foreign country
{Gamdang}, foreign land, with the intensifier <pi>: a land wholly foreign to a person.
<gamdang> and <sum> written as one word: the money of another country
<gamdang> and <tawh> written as one word: with another country, with foreign lands
Plural of <gamdang>: other countries and their peoples, the nations.
<gam>, the land outside the village, with <dawi>, spirit: a spirit of the wild, called on to go home when the spirits are driven out at <Khuado>

terms: as far as the land/down to the realm
definition: <Gam>, land, with <dong>, until: as far as the land or realm of, in the verse the realm of the dead.
<Gam>, land, with <dung>, length; paired with <gamvai>, the breadth of the land.
a game that is played, mostly a video game or a match in sport; {Game kimawl} is to play a game
the English word game and <sai.3>, shop, not elephant: a shop with gaming machines or computer games where customers pay to play, in the news from Malaysia a place where many migrants work
<gam>, country, repeated: each in its own land, the various countries, often beside <munmun>
placed after a verb: doing it with great force or heat, as {kiko gamgam}, shout loudly
<Gam>, land, with <gei>, side or edge; {sehnel gamgei} is the edge of the desert.
<Gam>, land, with <gi>, boundary: the border or limit of a land, of a city or of the sea.
<gamgi>, border, and <kikal>, between: the border between two countries or states, which are named before it and joined by <leh> or a dash; mostly followed by <ah>, on the border between them
<gamgi>, border, with <cing>, guard, written as one word: guarding the border; {gamgicing galkap} is border guard troops and {gamgicing in om} is be stationed guarding the border
<gamgi>, border, and <dung>, length, written as one word: the land along a border, along the border
Plural of <gamgi>: the borders of a land, and so the land within them.

bamboo, <gua>, that grows in the forest, set against <inngua>, the bamboo by the house; the saying {inngua hah lo gamgua hah}, clearing the wild bamboo and not the house bamboo, blames one who sees to others before his own
Land or property that is handed down in a family or tribe; {gamh luah} is to receive an inheritance.

terms: burn the land/set fire to the forest
definition: <gam>, land or wild country, with <hal>, burn
<gam>, country, with <hau>, rich, written as one word: a wealthy country
plural of <gamhau>: the wealthy countries, set against <gamzawngte>, the poor countries
{Gamh}, inheritance, with <luah>, inherit: land or possession received as a share to keep.
The person who inherits.
{Gamhluah}, inheritance, with the marker <in>: as an inheritance, for a possession.
{Gamhluah} with the noun suffix <na>: the land or place that a person or tribe has inherited.
{Gamhluah} with <pa>, which marks a man: the man who inherits.
{Gamhluah} with the plural <te>: those who inherit.
{Gamhluah} with the plural <te>: the shares of land that pass to the heirs.
<Gam>, land, with <hoih>, good: the good land that God promised.
<gamhoih>, good land, with <na>: a place where the land is good, which people head for when they move
treat others roughly and without respect; named together with <pheengtat> and with <totbawl>, provoke
violent or lawless behaviour; probably a spelling of <gamtatna>, conduct, used of bad conduct
Plural of <gamh>: the shares of land handed down in a tribe or family.
<gam>, land, with <huam>, the area taken in: the area that belongs to a town or a ruler; {Tedim gamhuam} is the Tedim area
<gam>, country, with <huang>, enclosure: the bounded area of a country or state
<Gam> with the marker <in> written together: as a country, or the land as the subject of the sentence.
<gam>, wild land, with <kang>, burn: a fire that burns the forest or the open land
<gam>, wild land or forest, with <katna>, burning: a fire that burns over forest or open country
<gam>, country, with <ke>, part: one of the large parts into which a country is divided, such as a state of the United States or India or a region of Myanmar
one of the parts into which a country is divided, with a government of its own: a state of a union or a province
<gam>, land, with <keek>, push out a border: one who seizes the land of others; placed before the name of a colonial power, as in {gamkeek Mikang kumpi}, the colonial British government
take the land of another people and rule it
those who take the land of other peoples and rule it, from <gam>, land, and <keek>, enlarge a border, with the plural <te>; {Mikang gamkeekte} are the British colonial rulers
<Gam>, wild country, with <keel>, goat: a wild goat.
Plural of <gamkeel>: wild goats.
a power that takes and rules the land of others, from <gam>, land; also the taking itself; {gamkek hun} is the colonial period and {gamkek kumpi} a colonial government
<gamkek> with the plural <te>: the colonial powers or rulers
<gamke>, state, with the plural <te>
<Gam>, land, with <keu>, dry: land without water.
said of the country in the hot season, when everything is dry and fire spreads easily; {gamkeu} is then the predicate, before <in> or <mahmah>, and not the name of a kind of land
<gam> and <keuna> written as one word: dry country, mostly before <mun>, as {sehnel gamkeuna mun}, a sandy desert place
a month of the traditional Zomi calendar, set beside June in the book's table of month names
<gam>, country, and <khangto>, grow or develop, written as one word: a developed country; {gamkhangto te} are the developed countries
<gamkhangto>, developed country, with the plural <te>: the developed countries
<Gam>, land or kingdom, written together with <khat>, one: one kingdom, a kingdom; <gamkhat leh gamkhat> is kingdom against kingdom.

terms: between countries/country and country/from country to country
definition: <gamkhat>, one country, said twice and joined by <leh>: one country and another, countries among themselves. Stands before a noun or verb of mutual dealing, as {gamkhat leh gamkhat kizopna}, relations between countries, and {gamkhat leh gamkhat kido}, country fights country, or before a thing that differs from one country to the next. The same pattern is made with other nouns and <khat>
<gamkhat>, a country or one country, and <in> written as one word: as a country of some kind, or together as one country
<gamkhat>, one country, and <pan>, from, written as one word; {gamkhatpan gamkhat} is from one country to another
<gamkhat>, one country, and the topic marker <pen>, written as one word: one country, as the thing spoken about
<gamkhat>, a country, with <peuh>, any
<gam>, country, and <khempeuh>, all, written as one word
<gam>, country, with <khen>, divide: one of the parts into which a country is divided, such as a state of India
The state of a place laid waste; related to <gamkhing>, desolation, and also written <gamkhinna>.
A land or place laid waste and left without people; {gamkhing suak} is become desolate and {gamkhing suaksak} is make desolate.
{Gamkhing}, wasteland, written with a capital as a name given to the land.
<Gamkhing>, desolate place, with the ending <in>: in a desolate state; with <om> it means lie desolate and with <bawl> make desolate.
<Gamkhing>, desolation, with the superlative <pen>: the most desolate of all.
The state of a place laid waste; related to <gamkhing>, desolation, and also written <gamkhin'na>.
<gam>, land, with <kuam>, valley: a valley region; {Sukkot gamkuam} is the Valley of Sukkoth
a stretch of country in general, not only a valley, as in {tenna gamkuam}, the area where a people lives, and {gamkuam golpi}, a great region
<gam>, country, with <kuan>, set out: a going out into the country, said of a hunting party, of soldiers on operation and of a group on a trip; {gamkuan te} are those who went out
<gam>, country, and <kumpi>, government, written as one word
far in place; with <a> before it and <panin> or <ah> after it, it is used as a noun: {a gamla panin} is from a distance, {a gamla-ah} is at a distance
wild country where no one lives; the land the Israelites crossed after leaving Egypt

terms: in the field/in the wilderness/in the open country
definition: <gamlak> with the place ending <a>, the short form of <ah>: that is in the field or wilderness; {gamlaka om gamsate} are the beasts of the field
<gamlak> with the place marker <ah>: in or into the field, the open country or the wilderness
<gamlak>, wild country, with <pi>, great: land left wild and empty; {gamlakpi suak} is become a wasteland
<gamlak> with the plural <te>: the wild, uncultivated parts of a land
<gamla>, far, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not far away; {tawh ki gamlalo} is not far from
<gamla>, far, and <lualo>, not very, written as one word; {tawh aki gamlalualo} is not far from

terms: region/part of the world/direction of a country
definition: <gam>, country, with <lam>, direction, written as one word: the lands lying in a direction, as {nitumna gamlam}, the West, or the direction of a named country
<gamla>, far, with <pen>, most; {leimong gamlapen} is the farthest end of the earth
<gamla>, far, with <pi>, great: at, to or from a great distance; <gamlapi-ah> is to a far place, {gamlapi panin} is from afar
<gam>, country, with <la>, song, and <pi>, great: the anthem of a country, named after the country; a different word from {gamlapi}, far away
<gamla> and the intensifier <pipi> written as one word: very far away
form of <gamla> used before another word; {a gamlat mah bangin} is as far as
<gamla> far in its form <gamlat> with the noun suffix <na>: how far away something is
<gamla>, far, with the comparative <zaw>
<gam>, country, and <leh>, and, written as one word; mostly in {gamleh minam}, country and people
<gam>, country, with <lei>, land: the land of a country or a people, one's own land
apparently <gam>, land, <le>, and, <lei>, earth, written as one word: the land and the ground
<gam>, land, with <lian>, great
<gam>, country, and <lianpi>, great, written as one word: a large and powerful country or territory
plural of <gamlian>: the large and powerful countries of the world
<gam> land with <lim> picture: a map of a country or of the world
<gam>, land, with <luah>, inherit: land or a share received as an inheritance
<gamluah>, inheritance, with the noun suffix <na>: the holding of land by inheritance
loud confused noise of a crowd or of battle

terms: be in uproar/make a commotion/be noisy
definition: be full of noise and disorder, said of a crowd, an army or a town
<gamlum> uproar with the suffix <in>; {gamlumin om} is be in an uproar
